newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-NEW YORKERS CELEBRATE YANKEES WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NEW YORKERS CELEBRATE YANKEES WIN.

text.p: Thousands of New Yorkers took to the streets in the early hours of Sunday to celebrate the Yankees' World Series victory over the Atlanta Braves and at least 10 people were arrested for disorderly conduct in various incidents, a police spokesman said.

He said two police officers suffered minor injuries when a crowd of people threw bottles from rooftops in the Bronx, a borough of New York City, as soon as the Yankees clinched their first World Series Championship since 1978.

The Yankees beat the Braves 3-2 in their sixth game on Saturday night to complete a remarkable comeback in the best-of-seven series by sweeping three games in Atlanta and taking one at home after opening with two demoralising losses at Yankee Stadium.
The police spokesman said some of the celebrations were boisterous and "people got out of hand," but there were no reports of rioting or people breaking into stores.

He said there were three arrests in Brooklyn and seven arrests outside Yankee Stadium to control unruly crowds. In Upper Manhattan where several thousand people gathered police were mobilised but no serious incidents were reported.
